To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) rudist-rich bodies in Coniacian–Campanian successions of central–southern Italy are the result of the interaction between rudists and the sedimentary environment; (b) rudists are the main skeletal component of the sediment, and their distribution and taphonomic features are related to the environmental conditions of the different sectors; (c) rudist-rich beds in high-energy environments (marginal shelves) are metric to kilometric in thickness and lateral extension,

the Coniacian to Lower Campanian rudist-rich successions of central-southeastern Italy were formed in shallow-water carbonate platforms with a ramp-like morphology, which were characterised by two main rudist-dominated depositional settings.

Rudist-rich successions in the Late Cretaceous carbonate shelves of central and southern Italy are characterized by two main depositional settings (i.e., end members) related to different environmental parameters.

the study of the rudist-rich successions that characterise the Coniacian and Lower Campanian shallow-water carbonate shelves in the southern Apennines (Italy).
the sedimentology and taphonomy of rudist-bearing successsions of southern Italy.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Coniacian to Lower Campanian rudist-bearing success of southern Italy represent an open shelf with a ramp-like morphological configuration.

the rudist lithosomes of southern Italy are not related to the development of a specific rudist facies, but rather they are related to the environmental conditions that prevailed in different shelf sectors.

the two end members are the result of a spectrum of depositional settings in which a large variety of rudist-rich lithofacies are recognised, ranging from high-energy to low-energy conditions, with intermediate successions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rudist-rich bodies in the studied successions are the expression of a wide range of environmental parameters, which were controlled by the position of the rudist colonies within the different shelf sectors.
rudist lithosomes were formed by the accumulation of rudist-derived debris, in a similar way to that of other bioclastic lithologies.
the rudist-bearing deposits of the southern Italian Cretaceous shelves are characterised by the presence of rudist-rich bodies, which can be recognised in different facies associations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the Coniacan-Lower Campanian of the southern Apennines, rudist-rich lithosomes are not the expression of the same depositional environment but of different settings, which can be recognised in terms of the sedimentary and taphonomic features of the rudist-bearing beds.
the rudist-rich successions are not the result of a single process.

, in contrast with the traditional view, rudist-rich deposits in shallow-water successions of central-southerm Italy are not necessarily associated with low-energy, restricted, protected shelf sectors.
